evals.prompt: Onboard Datadog for Bitrise mobile CI, AWS deployments, and DORA. We need exact evidence links but Datadog must not become our source of truth.
assertions: Defines consistent service/environment/version/repository/commit/pipeline/build/artifact/deployment mappings and preserves independent Bitrise, source-host, AWS, and Datadog opaque references
States that Datadog correlations/aggregates are views and do not replace authoritative source, build, deployment, cloud, or workflow identity
Tests retries, duplicate/late/failed/rolled-back/out-of-band deployments, incomplete mappings, outages, rollback, and fresh-context reference resolution

evals.prompt: Enable Datadog LLM Observability for an internal agent. Default to no prompt, completion, tool output, source, secrets, or personal data. Show how to verify privacy and cost.
assertions: Uses metadata-only collection by default and requires separate declared purpose/authorization before sensitive content capture
Previews fields/content, pre-egress redaction, sampling, retention, residency, access, deletion/export, downstream use, volume and cost budget
Uses prohibited-data canaries plus allowed-metadata, role-denial, sampling/retention, outage/backpressure, deletion, rollback, and drift probes

evals.prompt: Configure Datadog AWS integration, Cloud Security, Audit Trail, and Software Catalog. Can Datadog findings replace CloudTrail and own service metadata automatically?
assertions: Rejects replacing AWS CloudTrail/Config/Security Hub or authoritative target state with Datadog observations and keeps their native references separate
Requires an explicit Software Catalog source of truth and prevents observed telemetry tags from silently overwriting ownership
Previews least-privilege AWS role/external trust, accounts/regions/resources/data/cost, finding/audit access/retention, verification, rollback, and drift

evals.prompt: Set up credentials for a service that reads Datadog dashboards and for a browser that submits RUM events. Explain which Datadog key types to use, how to scope and verify them, and how their lifecycle should be managed.
assertions: Uses an organization API key plus a least-privilege service-account application key for server-side API access, and a client token rather than either secret key in the browser
Names the DD-API-KEY and DD-APPLICATION-KEY headers and verifies the key pair against the selected Datadog site, including bounded handling of propagation delay
Hands provider-neutral secret storage, runtime injection, rotation, and exposure response to credential-management-guide instead of duplicating that lifecycle locally
